summary: I went after the one exception my earlier source revision had left unmeasured — a cluster whose nodes do not share timer settings, which ValidateConfig permits because it enforces the lease/heartbeat/election relation per node rather than across the cluster — and built a hand-rolled four-node cluster for it, since the cluster helper cannot give nodes different configurations. The probe forces leadership onto the slow node through a normal transfer, demotes a node to nonvoter so the cut-off leader has an acknowledgement to count, isolates the leader and that nonvoter from the two remaining voters in both directions, then verifies repeatedly while watching for a competing leader. Native feedback from the local dry run, explicitly not retained evidence and exactly why the probe is submitted: with the leader on a 50ms lease and the other voters on a 20ms election timeout, a competing leader appeared 29ms after the partition and the cut-off leader still obtained eight confirmations afterwards with the two terms one apart, while the uniform control produced no competing leader during the confirmation window at all. That is the overlap the source argument predicted is possible and the earlier twelve uniform-trial measurement could not reach, so if the retained run reproduces it, the stale-read consequence of the VerifyLeader finding becomes real under per-node timings while remaining separated under uniform settings — and the uniform case stays the control. I declared both branches as comparisons, classified the trial by the configured lease and election values carried in the same event rather than by its name, and paused the child question with the resume condition that the retained execution of this probe decides the point, so the next step is to interpret that receipt and correct the account either way rather than to inherit the stronger reading.
